extracted.intended_audience: program managers, Navy personnel, and analysts conducting site/location evaluations and OMB A-76 cost comparisons for the HRMIN system
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation rubric and cost-comparison methodology for selecting an operational residence (site) for the Human Resource Management Information Network (HRMIN), using criteria prioritized by program managers/users and the OMB A-76 cost-comparison framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: System Performance and Reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: System performance was defined as how well the system supports and performs the function of the application running on it. System reliability was defined as the ability of a system to provide dependable support on a continuous basis (90% up-time and a back-up system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion is listed first (highest importance) by Navy personnel interviewed. High rating implies good performance and reliability; example metric: 90% uptime plus backup. Used to compare alternatives (e.g., in-house vs timesharing).

rubrics_metrics.name: System and Data Security
rubrics_metrics.description: Security was defined as providing an acceptable level of protection against unauthorized access to the system and to HRM Survey data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second-most important criterion. Evaluate protection mechanisms for both system access and sensitive survey data; consider vendor vs in-house controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Control
rubrics_metrics.description: The key management control factor for any alternative is the ease with which the sponsor can monitor the performance of the system and if necessary re-direct the management or content of the application so that the plans or objectives for the system are effectively used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessability and ease of sponsor oversight; higher ratings when sponsor can readily monitor, re-direct, or influence operations/content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and Operational Support
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability of the managing organization at the location to provide adequate personnel resources for the maintenance and operation of the system hardware and software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate staffing, local expertise, transition time for new management, and anticipated maintenance contracts; in-house advantage if original developers remain (e.g., NPRDC wrote the software).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost was the final criterion used to evaluate the alternative locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legend notes: 'A HIGH RATING FOR THIS CATEGORY MEANS LOWER COSTS; HIGH IS COST-BENEFICIAL.' Cost is assessed using the OMB Circular No. A-76 cost-comparison framework; cost differences can determine whether contract-out or in-house is more economical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses of Economic Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic analysis is used in two ways: to assess the economic consequences of a decision already made, or as part of the decisionmaking process (to compare the economic consequences of two or more alternatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit which use case the analysis serves (assessment vs choice). The chapter's cost comparison is of the first case (assessing an existing in-house decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB A-76 low-bid/comparison rule
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular No. A-76 requires the 'low bid' be used when conducting a cost comparison and states: when the basic contract price exceeds the total in-house costs it can be assumed that the cost of in-house performance will be less than the cost of contracting-out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contract price > in-house cost, you may assume in-house performance is less costly and need not complete contract-out cost portions except for narrow exceptions (e.g., potential federal income taxes, asset disposal proceeds). Include contract administration additives (e.g., 4%) when comparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Elements (high-level list per OMB A-76)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost elements used in comparison: (1) Direct Labor; (2) Fringe Benefits on Labor; (3) Operations Overhead Expenses; (4) Other Direct Costs; (5) General and Administrative Expenses; (6) Inflation; (7) Cost of Capital; and (8) One-Time and Other Costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these elements as the structured checklist for accumulating total in-house or contract-out costs. Note which elements are germane to the base-year comparison (inflation and one-time costs may be excluded in some base-year analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct labor cost accumulation: use representative 'real' direct labor costs based on positions required for an operational system rather than prorated development-hour figures; FY82 example: $117,845.50 (estimate) vs $125,261.72 (actual prorated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate positions required for steady-state operation and compute annual labor charges accordingly; avoid underestimating by relying solely on development-hour prorations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe Benefits on Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefit costs (FY82 example $31,357.55). For the analysis all employees assumed permanent GS employees, not subject to FICA, no premium holiday pay, eligible for retirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define employee classification assumptions clearly; fringe rates must match personnel assumptions used for direct labor estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations Overhead Expenses (aggregate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations overhead consists of multiple sub-elements (indirect labor; indirect materials and supplies; depreciation; rent; maintenance and repair; support costs; utilities; insurance) summed into an operations overhead total (FY82 example total $124,580.00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either break out sub-elements for granularity or apply an appropriate aggregate. Identify items allocated into G&A vs direct overhead. Document sources (budgets, contracts) and assumptions for estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervision by the manager and user training are considered direct labor; other indirect labor attributed to performance is accounted for in the aggregate General and Administrative (G&A) Expenses total (N/A in the operations overhead breakout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify which supervisory/training activities are treated as direct vs indirect; ensure consistency with G&A allocation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Materials and Supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating supplies (computer paper, paper clips, pens, etc.) aggregated into General and Administrative Expenses. FY82 example applied to HRMIN: Code 205 (System Manager) $2,930.00; Code 16 (Research Psychologist) $5,132.00; total $8,062.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate small supply items but document allocations by cost center; do not omit minor recurring items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Straight-line depreciation used to spread cost of tangible capital assets over estimated useful life (author assumed five years). Tangible assets considered: HARRIS minicomputer, CDC disk drives, terminals. FY82 depreciation total $76,406. Note: some capital costs may be 'sunk' and excluded if already government-owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State depreciation method and useful life assumptions explicitly; identify sunk costs vs those to include in ongoing cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rent
rubrics_metrics.description: Rent is accounted for in the aggregate General and Administrative Expenses total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When present, include facility rent charges in G&A allocations; if rent is not applicable, state N/A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and Repair
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance contract to keep equipment operating: FY82 charge $34,000; estimate $40,000 in FY84 and FY84 estimate used to be representative of operational costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representative operational-year maintenance estimates rather than one-off historical figures; reflect expected increases over time when more representative figures available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Support costs are accounted for in the aggregate General and Administrative Expenses total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document what is included in support (help-desk, administrative support) and ensure proper allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility costs are accounted for in the aggregate General and Administrative Expenses total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include power, communications facility utilities where material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost of Government being self-insured for this operation is calculated using an 'insurance factor' (example factor = .0006 x total; FY example $112.00 per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute insurance/self-insurance charges per applicable government accounting factors; may be immaterial but should be included or explicitly excluded with rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Direct Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains royalties (SPSS software annual royalty), travel, training, and telecommunication services. FY82 examples: SPSS royalty $2,500 rising to $3,500; travel $1,950; training $8,000; telecommunications ~ $3,500/month ($42,000/yr).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telecommunications are user-sensitive (fixed + variable); highlight sensitivity: a doubling of use could increase yearly cost by about $18,000 in the example. Include software license fees, travel, and training explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: General and Administrative Expenses (G&A)
rubrics_metrics.description: G&A expense pool charges a portion to each cost center; example G&A cost elements by code: Code 205 $17,268.00 and Code 16 $14,219.00; total FY82 G&A $31,487.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use actual accounting pool allocations where available; break down by cost center codes for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation (treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inflation is not germane to a base year cost comparison; the author has no reason to suspect inflation rates will differ by performance possibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether inflation adjustments are needed based on whether multi-year comparisons are being made; for single base-year comparisons, inflation may be excluded with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of Capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempts to determine opportunity cost (if capital had not been devoted to this performance it could have been used elsewhere). Example calculation: net book value $227,848 x opportunity cost rate 10% = $22,785.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include opportunity cost when relevant; state the rate and book values used and justify choice (e.g., 10% as imputed transfer cost from private to public sector).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-Time and Other Costs (treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: One-time and other costs are not appropriate to this chapter because it is assessing an existing in-house performance; they are excluded from the base-year comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether one-time conversion/disposal costs should be included depending on whether analysis is forward-looking or strictly base-year assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation / Sunk Cost Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Some capital costs are treated as sunk and not considered because by the time of publication the capital will be owned by the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly declare which capital costs are sunk vs current and exclude sunk costs from incremental cost comparisons when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking and User-Profile Adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmarking of vendor timesharing costs used typical SPSS programs and estimated utilization (connect time, on-line storage, batch processing). Adjust vendor benchmark connect/processing time by a factor determined from a 'real' in-house usage profile (example: Tymshare 'worst case' 13,695 hours divided by postulated 4,740 hours gave adjustment factor 2.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use actual host job-accounting and external connect logs to derive representative usage; compute adjustment factor to scale vendor benchmark hours to realistic in-house usage; document assumptions (e.g., processing time proportional to connect time).

rubrics_metrics.name: User Profile Determination and Data Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use HARRIS job accounting reports and Tymnet records (examples: Sep–Dec 1982 allocated time and CPU time) to determine total system usage and derive 'real' yearly connect time (example result 4,740.5 hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer contemporaneous host accounting and network connect logs; do not assume benchmarked vendor usage equals actual usage without adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity Analysis and Assumptions Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis highlights sensitivity of certain costs (telecommunications, connect time) and states intangible costs such as cost of capital and insurance are too small to be material. Recommends repeating study when historical usage patterns are documented (about five years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct sensitivity checks on major cost drivers; explicitly state assumptions and materiality thresholds; plan to revisit analysis after sufficient operational history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net Present Value (NPV) Analysis (briefed but constrained)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present value analysis discounts future cash flows to present value to compare alternatives over time. For government investments present value may be less germane; a 10% discount rate is used to represent opportunity cost rather than literal government return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performing multi-year comparisons, state discount rate and rationale (here, 10% as opportunity cost). Be careful applying discount percentages directly to lump-sum cost totals if different cash-flow timing exists; follow standard discounted cash flow procedures.
